env GO111MODULE=on
env GOPROXY=off

[!compiler:gc] skip
[short] skip

# Outside of GOROOT, our vendored packages should be reported as part of the standard library.
go list -f '{{if .Standard}}{{.ImportPath}}{{end}}' std cmd
stdout ^vendor/golang\.org/x/net/http2/hpack
stdout ^cmd/vendor/golang\.org/x/arch/x86/x86asm
! stdout ^golang\.org/x/

# The dependencies of those packages should also be vendored.
go list -deps vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/chacha20
stdout ^vendor/golang\.org/x/crypto/internal/alias

# cmd/... should match the same packages it used to match in GOPATH mode.
go list cmd/...
stdout ^cmd/compile
! stdout ^cmd/vendor/golang\.org/x/arch/x86/x86asm

# GOROOT/src/... should list the packages in std as if it were a module
# dependency: omitting vendored dependencies and stopping at the 'cmd' module
# boundary.

go list $GOROOT/src/...
stdout ^bytes$
! stdout ^builtin$
! stdout ^cmd/
! stdout ^vendor/
! stdout ^golang\.org/x/


# Vendored dependencies should appear with their 'vendor/' paths in std (they're
# in GOROOT/src, but not in the 'std' module following the usual module-boundary
# rules).

cd $GOROOT/src
env GOWORK=off

go list std
stdout ^vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack
! stdout ^golang\.org/x

# The dependencies of packages with an explicit 'vendor/' prefix should
# still themselves resolve to vendored packages.
go list -deps vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/chacha20
stdout ^vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/internal/alias
! stdout ^golang\.org/x

# Within the std module, the dependencies of the non-vendored packages within
# std should appear to be packages beginning with 'vendor/', not 'golang.org/…'
# module dependencies.

go list all
! stdout ^golang.org/x/
! stdout ^std/
! stdout ^cmd/
stdout ^vendor/

go list -deps -f '{{if not .Standard}}{{.ImportPath}}{{end}}' std
! stdout .

# The std module should not default to -mod=vendor: explicitly-added
# requirements should use module resolution instead of GOROOT/src/vendor.

cp go.mod $WORK/std.mod
go mod edit -modfile=$WORK/std.mod -droprequire=golang.org/x/crypto -droprequire=golang.org/x/mod -droprequire=golang.org/x/net -droprequire=golang.org/x/sync -droprequire=golang.org/x/sys -droprequire=golang.org/x/term -droprequire=golang.org/x/text -droprequire=golang.org/x/tools
go mod edit -modfile=$WORK/std.mod -require=example.com/dep@v1.0.0 -replace=example.com/dep@v1.0.0=$WORK/dep
go list -modfile=$WORK/std.mod -f '{{.Dir}}' example.com/dep
stdout $WORK[/\\]dep

# Workspaces including std should also use normal module resolution.

cd $WORK
go work init $GOROOT/src ./dep
env GOWORK=$WORK/go.work
cd $GOROOT/src
go list -f '{{.Dir}}' example.com/dep
stdout $WORK[/\\]dep
env GOWORK=off

# With an explicit -mod=vendor, the 'golang.org/…' module dependencies should
# resolve to the vendored directories.

go list -mod=vendor -f '{{.Dir}}' golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack
stdout $GOROOT[/\\]src[/\\]vendor

# Within the std module, the packages within the module should omit the 'std/'
# prefix (they retain their own identities), but should respect normal module
# boundaries (vendored packages are not included in the module, even though they
# are included in the 'std' pattern).

go list ./...
stdout ^bytes$
! stdout ^builtin$
! stdout ^cmd/
! stdout ^vendor/
! stdout ^golang\.org/x/


# Within std, the vendored dependencies of cmd should still appear to be part of cmd.

go list -mod=vendor -f '{{if .Standard}}{{.ImportPath}}{{end}}' cmd
stdout ^cmd/vendor/golang\.org/x/arch/x86/x86asm

go list -mod=vendor -f '{{if not .Standard}}{{.ImportPath}}{{end}}' cmd
! stdout .

go list -mod=vendor cmd/...
stdout ^cmd/compile
! stdout ^cmd/vendor/golang\.org/x/arch/x86/x86asm

-- $WORK/dep/go.mod --
module example.com/dep
-- $WORK/dep/dep.go --
package dep
